items.title: Google February 2026 Discover core update is now complete
items.summary: Google's February 2026 Discover core update, which rolled out over 21 days starting February 5, has completed and is the first announced Discover-only update, impacting only English-language users in the U.S. with plans to expand globally. It prioritizes locally relevant content from U.S.-based websites, reduces clickbait and sensational material, and highlights in-depth, original, timely content from sites with topic-specific expertise. This shift may affect Discover traffic for non-U.S. sites targeting U.S. audiences and emphasizes personalized content based on user preferences.

items.title: Straight From the (AI) Source: Is AEO/GEO different than SEO? Google, Microsoft, and others explain how to be visible in AI search
items.summary: The article compiles direct insights from Google, Microsoft, and Perplexity on AI search visibility, emphasizing that traditional SEO practices form the foundation for AEO/GEO, with no need for entirely new tactics. Google representatives like Danny Sullivan and John Mueller state that good SEO covers AI search optimization, focusing on user-focused content, originality, and avoiding spammy methods like content chunking. AI search uses RAG to ground responses in search engines, reinforcing the importance of crawlability, structured data, and clear content for visibility across platforms like AI Overviews and Copilot.

items.title: From Rankings to References: The Structural Shift from SEO to AEO
items.summary: Google rankings are now just one of several interfaces for brand discovery, with AI-generated answers quickly becoming the default, necessitating the addition of answer engine optimization (AEO) to existing SEO campaigns. While traditional SEO tactics like topical authority and high-quality backlinks can support AEO, specific AI visibility gaps can render brands invisible even if they dominate keyword rankings. This shift is driven by trends such as AI Overviews reducing click-through rates by up to 58% and 72% of searchers using AI features, making AEO adoption essential for maintaining online visibility.

items.title: How Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol changes ecommerce SEO
items.summary: Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), launched on January 11, enables AI agents to discover, evaluate, recommend, and purchase products within Google's AI experiences like AI Mode and Gemini. This shifts ecommerce from site-based selling to AI-driven transactions, where visibility depends on product feeds, structured data, and Merchant Center integration rather than traditional rankings. Optimization now focuses on complete attributes in feeds (e.g., titles, descriptions, GTINs, images, use cases), aligning with structured data on sites, and connecting Search Console to Merchant Center for monitoring diagnostics, performance, and alerts.

items.title: Literary Agents Reject AI-Generated Submissions
items.summary: Several literary agencies have amended their submission guidelines to explicitly reject cover letters and manuscripts created with generative AI, noting a detectable change in the nature of recent submissions. Agents report that AI-assisted work lacks the authenticity they seek and is easier to identify. This policy shift underscores growing concerns over AI's role in writing and publishing.

items.title: Big Five Publishers Target BookTok Self-Published Hits
items.summary: The Big Five publishers are acquiring self-published books that have succeeded on BookTok, with 93 deals in 2025 for existing works, mostly in romance and romantasy. This strategy uses proven sales data to reduce risk and secure multi-book contracts. Indie success on the platform is reshaping traditional acquisition paths.

items.title: Harlequin Closes Historical Romance Line After 40 Years
items.summary: Harlequin is shuttering its historical romance imprint by fall 2027, as indie authors dominate via Kindle Unlimited with superior royalties and speed. Traditional publishing's slower model has lost market share in romance genres. The closure signals a broader shift favoring self-publishing.

items.title: Conservative Leaders Release Books on Espionage and Public Service
items.summary: David Shedd, former intelligence officer, co-authored 'The Great Heist' detailing China's campaign to steal U.S. secrets, while Don Hodel's autobiography 'Called to Serve' recounts his Reagan cabinet service and faith-driven career. Announced February 24, 2026, by Patrick Henry College. The releases highlight themes of national security and traditional leadership.

items.title: Researchers Extract 95.8% of Harry Potter from Claude AI Model
items.summary: Stanford and Yale researchers extracted nearly the entire text of 'Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone' word-for-word from Anthropic's Claude 3.7 Sonnet, and substantial portions from Gemini 2.5 Pro and others. Models reproduced novels from memory without always needing jailbreaks, costing as little as $2 per book. Findings challenge AI firms' claims of pattern learning over memorization, fueling copyright debates.

items.title: HQ Signs Two-Book Deal with Crime Author Nadine Matheson
items.summary: HarperCollins imprint HQ acquired UK and Commonwealth rights to two new crime novels by Nadine Matheson. The deal continues the author's momentum in the genre following previous successes. Announced two days ago.

items.title: Scary Movie 6 Trailer Sparks Outrage for Mocking Woke Pronouns
items.summary: The trailer for the upcoming Scary Movie 6 includes a scene where a stabbing victim corrects bystanders on pronouns, saying 'Not HER! My pronouns are they/them. He stabbed THEM!' This has ignited online backlash with some labeling it transphobic and outdated. Others hail it as a refreshing return to the series' irreverent humor.

items.title: A Knight of Seven Kingdoms Actress Responds to Racial Casting Backlash
items.summary: Tanzyn Crawford, cast as Tanselle in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, addressed online backlash targeting her race for the role. She described entering the franchise as intimidating amid the negativity but confirmed support from George R.R. Martin, who said she fit his vision. The incident underscores fan reactions to casting choices in fantasy adaptations.

items.title: BAFTA Faces Backlash After Man with Tourette's Shouts N-Word Onstage
items.summary: At the BAFTA awards, activist John Davidson, who has Tourette's syndrome and inspired a nominated film, involuntarily shouted the N-word and profanities during a presentation by Black actors Michael B. Jordan and Delroy Lindo for Sinners. BAFTA issued apologies, but actors like Wendell Pierce demanded more, while later NAACP Image Awards featured jokes mocking the white disabled man. The event sparked debates on context, apologies, and double standards.

items.title: Susan Sarandon Claims She's Blacklisted from Hollywood Over Gaza Remarks
items.summary: Susan Sarandon stated her agents fired her for protesting and speaking on Gaza, barring her from TV and major films in America. She now works on smaller European indies amid similar casting hurdles. The revelation points to repercussions for outspoken activism in entertainment.

items.title: BAFTA Tourette's Incident Draws Mixed Reactions and Apologies
items.summary: John Davidson's uncontrollable outburst at BAFTAs, including the N-word toward Sinners presenters, led to host apologies and actor criticisms. Production designer Hannah Beachler dismissed further apologies as unnecessary. Coverage highlighted varying responses to the profanity linked to the medical condition.

items.title: Scary Movie 6 Sinners Parody Rumored to Feature Controversial Blackface Imagery
items.summary: Reports suggest the Scary Movie 6 parody of Sinners may include Ghostface mask with blackface elements, potentially sparking further debate. This comes amid existing backlash to the trailer's pronoun gag. The franchise continues its tradition of satirical horror spoofs.

items.title: 5 AI Tools That Can Practically Run Your Business in 2026
items.summary: The article discusses five AI tools that enable businesses, particularly small and midsize ones, to automate routine operational tasks like scheduling, research, documentation, and workflow coordination, thereby reducing manual work and improving efficiency. These tools act as digital collaborators for repetitive processes, allowing teams to focus on higher-value decisions while maintaining human oversight for critical tasks. The tools are ChatGPT, Lindy.ai, Motion, Zapier AI, and Fireflies.ai.

items.title: Workplace AI: SMBs are automating these key tasks in 2026
items.summary: SMBs are increasingly using AI to automate tasks like market research (55%), scheduling and calendar management (55%), data analysis (52%), and inventory management (52%) to combat rising operating expenses, with 10% already employing automation for this purpose. The survey of 322 US SMBs also shows 13% spending over 41% of monthly revenue on operating expenses, highlighting the financial pressures driving AI adoption.

items.title: How AI can supercharge small business growth
items.summary: QuickBooks uses AI and machine learning to analyze anonymized data from millions of customers to provide small businesses with insights on revenue flow, expenses, tax payments, and payroll for better decision-making. Key features include Cash Flow Planner predicting cash flow up to 90 days ahead, faster payments, and Live Bookkeeping with professionals. This helps small businesses manage operations proactively and improve success rates.

items.title: 2026 Small Business Resolutions: Expert AI Prompts Releases Productivity Roadmap
items.summary: Expert AI Prompts has released a free guide titled “5 Expert AI Prompts That Save 5 Hours This Week,” designed to help small business owners save five hours weekly using advanced AI prompts for tasks like client emails and social media. The guide provides structured frameworks for immediate workflow integration. It supports 2026 AI adoption for solopreneurs.

items.title: Trace raises $3M to solve the AI agent adoption problem
items.summary: Trace raised $3 million in seed funding to build a knowledge graph from enterprise tools like email and Slack, enabling AI agents to handle tasks with context. Its workflow orchestration delegates between agents and humans, automating processes like onboarding. This positions Trace as infrastructure for agentic AI in business.
